title: Dedicated owner account
unblocks: every other signup below; recovery when a sign-in lockout hits on day 1

steps.action: Create a business email used only for this project's services.
steps.expect: The new inbox receives a welcome message.

steps.action: Add a passkey on your own device, before many sign-in attempts can lock the new account.
steps.expect: The passkey is listed under sign-in methods.

steps.action: Generate backup codes and store them offline (printed or in a password manager).
steps.expect: The page shows the codes were generated, with a date.

steps.action: Add a recovery email you already control and confirm it.
steps.expect: The recovery email shows as verified.

title: Billing with hard spend caps
unblocks: paid tiers and API usage without a surprise bill or a mid-pilot suspension

steps.place: Each paid service → Billing page (hosting provider, database, AI provider, error monitor)
steps.action: Add a payment method and any required credit.
steps.expect: The billing page shows an active payment method and no unpaid balance.

steps.place: Each paid service → Billing → Spend limit or budget
steps.action: Set a hard monthly cap, not only an alert.
steps.expect: The cap is listed as active for the current month.

steps.action: Add an alert at 50% and 90% of the cap, sent to the owner account.
steps.expect: Two alert thresholds are listed with the owner email.

title: Domain and DNS
unblocks: the production URL, auth redirect URLs and mail sender verification

steps.action: Buy the production domain with the owner account.
steps.expect: The domain is listed under your domains with an expiry date and auto-renew on.

steps.action: Add the records your hosting provider and mail provider list for this domain.
steps.expect: Each record appears in the DNS records table.

steps.action: Add the domain and wait for verification.
steps.expect: The domain shows as verified with a valid certificate.

title: Error monitoring
unblocks: agents reading production errors without asking you for screenshots

steps.action: Create one project for this app and copy its DSN into the deploy environment.
steps.expect: The project page shows a DSN and 'waiting for first event'.

steps.action: Create a token with read-only scopes for agents and store it as a secret, not in the repo.
steps.expect: The token is listed with read-only scopes.

title: Legal minimum for a pilot
unblocks: inviting real people and collecting their data

steps.action: Name the processors (hosting, database, AI provider, error monitor), the operator's identity and contact, and how long data is kept.
steps.expect: The draft names every processor and a retention period.

steps.action: Describe a delete-my-data path that also removes the user's login, not only their rows.
steps.expect: The page states how to request deletion and that the account is removed.

steps.action: Publish the page and link it from the sign-up screen.
steps.expect: The page loads on the production domain and the sign-up screen links to it.

title: Pilot users and a definition of done
unblocks: a pilot with real feedback instead of an open-ended beta

steps.action: List 5-10 named pilot users and how each one is contacted.
steps.expect: Each name has a contact channel next to it.

steps.action: Write what 'pilot done' means: who, which tasks, for how long.
steps.expect: One paragraph states measurable exit criteria.

title: Custom SMTP for auth mail
unblocks: invites and password resets to anyone outside the team

steps.action: Add the sending domain and copy its DNS records into Domain registrar → DNS records.
steps.expect: The mail provider shows the domain as verified.

steps.place: Mail provider → API keys or SMTP credentials
steps.action: Create SMTP credentials for the auth service.
steps.expect: A host, port, username and password are shown once; save them in your secret store.

steps.action: Enable custom SMTP with those credentials before the first real invite; the built-in mailer is rate-limited or team-only.
steps.expect: A test invite to an address outside the team arrives within a minute.

title: OAuth consent screen and verification
unblocks: sign-in with the OAuth provider for pilot users who are not test users

steps.action: Create the consent screen in testing mode with the app name, support email, privacy URL and only the scopes you use.
steps.expect: The consent screen shows publishing status 'Testing'.

steps.place: OAuth provider console → Consent screen → Test users
steps.action: Add every pilot user's email as a test user; testing-mode tokens expire in days, so plan re-consent.
steps.expect: Each pilot email is listed under test users.

steps.place: OAuth provider console → Consent screen → Publish / Submit for verification
steps.action: Submit for verification early; review can take weeks for sensitive scopes.
steps.expect: The status shows verification pending or in review.

title: Payment provider business account
unblocks: taking real payments and live webhooks

steps.place: Payment provider → Sign up → Business account
steps.action: Create the account with the owner email and the business's legal details.
steps.expect: The dashboard opens in test mode.

steps.action: Submit identity and bank details now; verification can take days.
steps.expect: The status shows verification submitted or pending review.

title: AI provider key with a monthly cap
unblocks: AI features in preview and production without unbounded spend

steps.action: Set a hard monthly cap for the operator account, or record in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md that users bring their own key.
steps.expect: The hard limit is shown for the current month, or the bring-your-own-key decision is written down.

steps.place: AI provider → API keys → Create key
steps.action: Create an operator key scoped to this project and store it as a deploy secret, not in the repo.
steps.expect: The key is listed with the project name and a last-used of 'never'.

title: VM ingress: cloud rule and host firewall
unblocks: reaching the app on the VM from the internet

steps.place: Cloud console → Networking → Security list or security group for the VM
steps.action: Add an ingress rule for the app port from the sources you need.
steps.expect: The rule is listed under ingress rules.

steps.action: Open the same port in the host firewall too; the cloud rule alone is not enough.
steps.expect: The firewall status lists 443/tcp as allowed.

steps.action: Persist the host rule so it survives a reboot, then reboot once to check.
steps.expect: After the reboot, https://example.com answers from outside the VM.
